name: browser_exec
description:
Run Python in a persistent browser session (variables survive across calls); returns what the code prints. This instance has ONE real Chromium shared by every agent on it, and the user can watch it live.
START WITH THESE (pre-loaded):
- elements(): print the current page as a numbered list of clickable/typeable elements plus its visible text. Use it to read the page and find things.
- act(n): click [n]; act(n, 'text', enter=True): replace field [n]'s text (optionally press Enter); act(n) on a 'select … → "option"' row picks that option; act('down') / act('up') scroll. act() re-checks the page before touching it and prints the new list afterwards.
BATCH: when the list already shows everything the next steps need, do them in ONE call — e.g. act(1, 'Alice', observe=False); act(2, '555', observe=False); act(5, observe=False); act(9) — only the last one prints the new list. A step that fails prints 'Not done' and returns False; stop there and look again. Do not spend one call per field or checkbox.
Navigation: new_tab(url) for the first page, then goto_url(url); wait_for_load(). After new_tab / switching tabs run cdp('Page.bringToFront') before taking a screenshot.
The user watches this browser live: leave your last page open — never close_tab() at the end.
Lower level when needed: js(code), cdp(method, **params), list_tabs(), switch_tab(), upload_file(), iframe_target(), page_info().
There is NO navigate tool and NO Playwright / browser_use.Browser / page.* API here — do not import them.

name: browser_screenshot
description: Capture the current page of the shared browser and return it as an image. Run cdp('Page.bringToFront') in browser_exec first if you just opened or switched a tab. Do not pass full=True unless you really need the whole page — it is much larger.

max_dim.description: Downscale so no side exceeds this many pixels
